items.headline: Trump announces Russia-Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' as strikes continue
items.summary: President Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed to stop attacking each other's energy infrastructure but gave no details. President Zelenskyy welcomed the announcement but said Russia was still striking energy facilities in Kyiv and Kharkiv.

items.headline: Riyadh airport struck again a day after deadly attack
items.summary: A projectile hit Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Sunday, a day after a missile strike there killed 12 people. The attack came shortly after the Houthis said Sanaa's airport had been hit again and blamed Saudi Arabia.

items.headline: Iran rejects latest U.S. proposal to end war as 'insufficient'
items.summary: A senior Iranian official said the latest U.S. response on ending the war falls short. In Israel, Prime Minister Netanyahu's corruption trial resumed with testimony from the former attorney general weeks before elections.

items.headline: Hurricane Simon slams Mexico's Pacific coast
items.summary: Hurricane Simon struck Mexico's Pacific coast as a Category 3 storm on Sunday, bringing strong winds and heavy rain to resort areas and vulnerable towns. The worst conditions were expected around Puerto Vallarta overnight into Monday.

items.headline: Isaias death toll rises to four as Rachel hits California
items.summary: At least four deaths are now linked to Isaias, which came ashore as a Category 2 hurricane near Destin, Florida, and is moving north. Meanwhile, the storm Rachel battered Southern California.

items.headline: Senators from both parties push back on Russian diesel deal
items.summary: Four Republican and two Democratic senators called on President Trump to reverse his plan to buy Russian diesel. They said the administration did not consult Congress or provide the justification required by law.

items.headline: At least 139 migrants die as boat capsizes off Djibouti
items.summary: A boat carrying migrants from Djibouti toward Yemen capsized, killing at least 139 people and leaving dozens missing, according to the International Organization for Migration. More than 80 Ethiopian nationals survived.

items.headline: Pope Leo XIV to have lung surgery this week
items.summary: Pope Leo XIV said he will undergo surgery this week after doctors found a nodule on his lung. He said it was detected early and is small and localized, and the Vatican expects about a week of recovery.

items.headline: Justice Department opens antitrust probe of TV networks
items.summary: The Justice Department is investigating TV networks over possible antitrust violations. The probe comes as a court fight continues over the White House barring some news outlets.

items.headline: Chinese drone limits squeeze police budgets
items.summary: U.S. restrictions on Chinese-made drones are driving up costs for police departments that rely on the inexpensive aircraft. Many departments with tight budgets have come to depend on the low-cost aircraft.

digest.overview:
Hurricane Isaias has now been linked to at least four deaths as it moves north from the Gulf Coast, while a separate storm, Rachel, battered Southern California. The Justice Department is investigating TV networks over possible antitrust violations as a court fight continues over barring some outlets from the White House. Four Republican and two Democratic senators urged President Trump to reverse his plan to buy Russian diesel, saying the administration skipped the consultation with Congress the law requires. Trump floated renaming the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean, extending his push to rename geographic features. Police departments say new U.S. limits on Chinese-made drones are driving up costs for the inexpensive aircraft they depend on.

Abroad, Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an "energy ceasefire," but President Zelenskyy said Russian strikes on energy sites in Kyiv and Kharkiv continued. Riyadh's King Khalid airport was hit again on Sunday, a day after a deadly strike, and Seoul urged South Koreans to leave Saudi Arabia. Iran called the latest U.S. proposal to end the war "insufficient," as Netanyahu's corruption trial resumed ahead of Israel's Oct. 27 election. North Korea fired several ballistic missiles toward the East Sea on Monday, one flying more than 900 kilometers, days after Seoul revealed a hypersonic glide vehicle test. South Korea's early-October exports hit a record $26.1 billion on surging chip sales. Pope Leo XIV will have surgery this week to remove a small lung nodule. At least 139 migrants died when a boat bound for Yemen capsized off Djibouti, and Hurricane Simon struck Mexico's Pacific coast as a Category 3 storm.

home.overview:
The Brewers struck first in the NLCS, beating the Dodgers 2–1 in Game 1 behind Brice Turang's homer and a shutdown bullpen as Tarik Skubal took the loss; Game 2 is today at 5 p.m. ET, and the ALCS opens tonight with Cleveland at Tampa Bay. In the NFL, Tyler Huntley's overtime sneak lifted the Ravens past the Falcons 30–23 on Sunday night, and the 49ers and Vikings both moved to 5–0. Cam Little's 57-yard field goal at the gun beat the Eagles 19–17 in London, the Packers forced five turnovers in a 31–7 rout of the Bears, and Arizona traded Marvin Harrison Jr. to Houston mid-game. The Bills visit the Rams on Monday Night Football.

Manchester City won 3–0 at Anfield after Ryan Gravenberch's red card and now lead Arsenal by three points, while Crystal Palace beat Forest 3–1 and Everton drew 2–2 at Hull. Real Betis put five past Osasuna, Freiburg went top of the Bundesliga on goal difference, and ten-man Southampton won the South Coast derby 1–0. St. Louis tied the MLS unbeaten record at 20 games with a 6–2 win over the Galaxy. The Champions League returns Tuesday and Wednesday, headlined by Man City–PSG and Roma–Real Madrid. In the KBO, Kia and LG are settling the No. 3 seed in today's regular-season finale.
